Subject: Zipper-tier consolidation — interpretation of floor smoothing & billing matrix

Diane — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick follow-up while the team digests the redline you shared: we want to make sure we have the same reading on two interlinked pieces (the "zipper" tier consolidation language in Exhibit B and the floor-smoothing clause in Schedule A) because they drive both invoice calculation and the minimum-commit true-up.

Two asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the seller-side interpretation of the zipper consolidation is that two adjacent tiers when combined will be billed at the weighted blended unit rate (per the proposed matrix), or whether the blended rate only applies when the combined monthly usage exceeds the higher tier threshold?
2) Relatedly, the floor-smoothing paragraph references an "annualized rollback" on commit shortfalls. Our finance team (cc'd) needs the billing matrix that defines how rollback is applied across months — is it pro-rata by invoice month or an annual true-up applied at the end of the term?

I've attached a cleaned excerpt of the pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_zipper_tiers.xlsx) that shows how we would calculate blend in both cases. If you prefer, Marissa can draft a short amendment that makes the fallback explicit.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if it's easier to talk through.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of GTM Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: pricing_matrix_zipper_tiers.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Diane Park <diane.park@acmecloud.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-07-07T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zipper-tier consolidation — interpretation of floor smoothing & billing matrix

Grace — thanks for the note and the matrix. Short answers first:
1) Our commercial team expects the blended unit rate to apply only when the combined monthly usage crosses the higher tier threshold. The intention behind that design is to prevent small month-to-month blending from eroding the tier protection we negotiated for predictability.
2) The annualized rollback is intended as an end-of-term true-up. We typically perform a single reconciliation against committed minima and apply any rollback/credit once per contract year. That's how we've handled similar accounts.

However, I understand this is operationally painful and could cause billing surprizes. Attached is our redline of Exhibit B where we (1) add a worked example and (2) propose an optional pro-rata monthly rollback as an appendix. Can you review the redline and flag anything that would materially affect your reporting?

Best,
Diane
Diane Park
Head of Procurement — Strategic Accounts
Acme Cloud

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_ExhibitB_redline_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Zipper-tier consolidation — interpretation of floor smoothing & billing matrix

Looping in Ben for ops/billing impact and Laura for invoice mapping (adding Laura now).

High level thoughts after a quick pass on Diane's answers and the attached redline:
- If Acme insists on the "blended only after crossing higher threshold" approach, that creates a discontinuity in monthly revenue recognition vs. usage smoothing for the customer. We can support it, but it increases the chance of a material step-change month for both billing and usage-based cost allocation.
- The end-of-term single reconciliation is simplest administratively but will push revenue risk to Redwood for intra-year shortfalls. A pro-rata monthly true-up reduces that risk but increases billing churn and dispute volume.

Operational ask: Ben, can you confirm whether our billing system can (a) compute weighted blends by month as per Grace's spreadsheet, and (b) toggle between pro-rata monthly true-ups vs annual true-up? If not, we need to pick the model that aligns with system capabilities.

—Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Zipper-tier consolidation — interpretation of floor smoothing & billing matrix

Marissa, Grace — quick ops readout:
- Our billing platform can compute weighted blends on a monthly basis with the matrix you provided. That will require a new calculation template but is doable within the current quarter.
- Toggling between monthly pro-rata true-up and annual true-up is not currently automated. We can implement the monthly true-up, but it will require: (1) a config flag per customer, (2) a reconciliation workflow change (automatic credit/charge memos), and (3) an extra dispute field so Customer Success can triage. Estimated delivery for the automation: 6–8 weeks (engineering + QA).

Operational recommendation: Offer Acme the pro-rata monthly true-up as a paid optionality (small monthly admin fee) or accept annual true-up but include a 30-day notice right for invoices that change by >10% in any month. That strikes a balance between their predictability needs and our dispute load.

Ben
Senior Billing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Zipper-tier consolidation — interpretation of floor smoothing & billing matrix

Diane — thanks for the redline and the example. After internal review:
- We can accept the blended-rate-only-after-crossing-higher-threshold approach, provided we add a short mechanism in Exhibit B that (a) includes a worked monthly example (we used your example, cleaned) and (b) sets a "monthly delta" notice threshold of 10% (if any invoice month varies >10% vs. forecasted blended calculation, Redwood issues a notice and both parties agree to pause automatic collection until dispute resolution).
- Regarding the rollback cadence: we'll sign with an annual true-up by default. As Ben outlined, we can enable the monthly pro-rata true-up as a paid add-on; I'll include optional language and a nominal admin fee line in the order form amendment.

Next steps: Marissa will produce a one-paragraph amendment and a final Excel snippet to attach to Exhibit B. Diane, if Acme agrees, we can incorporate and route a single DocuSign envelope. Planning note: if Acme opts into monthly pro-rata, Ben's team needs the configuration lead time (6–8 weeks) before the first invoice reflecting that model.

I'm attaching the cleaned pricing matrix and will follow up with the amendment draft in the next 24 hours.

—Grace
